title: Conditional Value of Graph Priors in Multi-Tracer Groundwater-Age Inference: A Hydrosheaf Benchmark of Public Aquifer Datasets
scope: A version upgrade of the accuracy-locked M3 benchmark paper for Applied Geochemistry. Reruns the residence-time and graph-prior benchmark of Hydrosheaf against the current codebase, verifies every locked statistic by regeneration rather than by inheritance, and adds two exploratory findings produced since the M3 lock: an independent set-valued compatibility audit of the graph-prior question, and an unresolved tracer-level local-infeasibility rate.

objectives.statement: Reproduce every M3-locked reportable statistic from the current codebase and disclose any numerical delta rather than assume the lock still holds.
acceptance_criteria: The full manuscript-analysis pipeline is rerun against current HEAD in an isolated copy
Every reportable statistic is diffed against the M3 lock manifest and the outcome is recorded in DECISIONS.md before any prose is drafted from it

objectives.statement: Evaluate whether physically plausible graph topology improves multi-tracer groundwater-age inference relative to single-well baselines and negative controls.
acceptance_criteria: A graph result is accepted only when RMSE improves, within-factor agreement does not deteriorate, and negative controls do not show a comparable effect
Reported ages are treated as model-derived reference products, not error-free true ages

objectives.statement: Test predictive graph value independently of reference-age agreement using leakage-guarded target-tracer withholding.
acceptance_criteria: The withheld tracer is excluded from fitting, graph construction and hyperparameter tuning for every graph node
Non-estimable comparisons (no eligible graph edges) are reported as non-estimable, not as equivalence

objectives.statement: Report the independent set-valued compatibility audit and the tracer-level local-infeasibility finding as exploratory diagnostics, without overstating them as confirmatory or field-validated.
acceptance_criteria: The audit is labelled exploratory/development-stage wherever it appears
No cause is asserted for the infeasibility rate; tested-and-rejected explanations are listed, not one favoured

objectives.statement: Give the reader a geographic sense of the benchmark's data coverage.
acceptance_criteria: A new study-area map shows the USGS public-supply sites used, by Principal Aquifer or study unit
The map does not imply field validation beyond the benchmarked release

inputs.provenance: M3 accuracy-locked results, 2026-07-28, commit 47fbf7c — baseline for comparison, not overwritten
Regenerated results from current HEAD, isolated copy of the M3 pipeline
Set-valued compatibility audit and infeasibility finding (exploratory, development-stage)
Seven-explanation exclusion protocol for the infeasibility signature

risks.risk: A regenerated number silently drifts from the M3-locked value without disclosure.
risks.mitigation: Every statistic is diffed against the M3 manifest before drafting; deltas are recorded in DECISIONS.md D2 and, if material, in the manuscript's own change note.

risks.risk: The exploratory set-valued audit is read as confirmatory or as validating true TTD recovery.
risks.mitigation: Labelled exploratory/development-stage at every mention; claim excluded explicitly in Outline.md.

risks.risk: The unresolved infeasibility rate is read as attributed to a specific cause.
risks.mitigation: All seven tested explanations are reported as rejected; no cause is asserted.

risks.risk: Reader-friendly rewriting of the main text loses a scientifically load-bearing caveat present in the locked M3 prose.
risks.mitigation: Every simplified main-text sentence is checked against its source section in the current M3 manuscript and the regenerated artifact_validation.json before being finalised.
